Introduction to Bits and Tricks.theory: An int has 32 bits in two's-complement form. `&` keeps common set bits, `|` combines bits, `^` differs bits, `~` flips bits. `1 << i` addresses bit i for 0<=i<32. Java masks shift distances modulo 32 for int and modulo 64 for long, so validate indices. `>>` sign-extends; `>>>` fills with zero. `n & (n-1)` clears the lowest set bit; `n & -n` isolates it. int bit patterns may be negative; interpret unsigned values with `Integer.toUnsignedLong` when needed.

Check if the i-th bit is Set or Not.problem: Use zero-based bit indices from the least-significant bit.
Check if the i-th bit is Set or Not.approach: Mask only bit i; a nonzero intersection means it was set.
Check if the i-th bit is Set or Not.complexity: O(1) for one fixed-width int; O(n) for array XOR/state scans. O(1) space.
Check if the i-th bit is Set or Not.pitfalls: Java int overflow and shifts operate on fixed 32-bit patterns here. Never shift by an unchecked index of 32; it would shift by zero.

Check if a Number is Odd or Not.approach: The least significant bit determines odd/even parity, including negatives.

Check if a Number is Power of 2 or Not.problem: Check whether a positive int is an integral power of two.
Check if a Number is Power of 2 or Not.approach: A positive power of two has exactly one set bit; clearing the lowest bit leaves zero.

Count the Number of Set Bits.approach: Brian Kernighan clears one set bit per iteration.

Set the Rightmost Unset Bit.approach: n+1 carries through trailing ones; OR retains the original ones and sets the first zero.

Swap Two Numbers.problem: Return swapped values; primitive caller variables cannot be mutated through method arguments.
Swap Two Numbers.approach: XOR swaps local copies without an extra integer temporary; returning an array communicates both results.
Swap Two Numbers.pitfalls: Prefer a temporary variable in normal Java code for readability. XOR-swapping an array entry with itself would zero it.

Minimum Bit Flips to Convert Number.problem: Count differing bits of two int patterns.
Minimum Bit Flips to Convert Number.approach: XOR is one exactly at differing positions; each needs one flip.
Minimum Bit Flips to Convert Number.complexity: O(1) for one fixed-width int; O(n) for array XOR/state scans. O(1) space.

Single Number - I.problem: Exactly one value occurs once and every other value twice.
Single Number - I.approach: Equal values cancel under XOR; order does not matter.
Single Number - I.complexity: O(1) for one fixed-width int; O(n) for array XOR/state scans. O(1) space.
Single Number - I.pitfalls: Java int overflow and shifts operate on fixed 32-bit patterns here. Never shift by an unchecked index of 32; it would shift by zero.

Single Number - II.problem: Exactly one value occurs once; every other value occurs three times.
Single Number - II.approach: Each bit has a finite-state count modulo three, represented by once/twice. Third occurrence clears the bit.
Single Number - II.complexity: O(1) for one fixed-width int; O(n) for array XOR/state scans. O(1) space.
Single Number - II.trace: For 2 its bit cycles once -> twice -> neither; 3 remains once.
Single Number - II.pitfalls: Java int overflow and shifts operate on fixed 32-bit patterns here. Never shift by an unchecked index of 32; it would shift by zero.

Single Number - III.problem: Exactly two distinct values occur once; every other value occurs twice. Return the two singletons sorted.
Single Number - III.approach: XOR all gives p^q, which is nonzero. A set bit differs between p and q; partition on that bit so repeated values cancel within each group.
Single Number - III.pitfalls: Signed MIN_VALUE can be an isolated bit; `(x&bit)!=0` remains correct. The input multiplicity contract is essential.

Divide two numbers without multiplicatio.problem: Compute quotient truncating toward zero without multiplication, division or remainder. Clamp the sole int-overflow quotient to MAX_VALUE.
Divide two numbers without multiplicatio.approach: Subtract the largest fitting power-of-two multiple of divisor at each bit from high to low; set that quotient bit. The remainder decreases while the reconstructed quotient accounts for every subtraction.
Divide two numbers without multiplicatio.complexity: 32 iterations: O(1) for fixed-width inputs, O(1) space.
Divide two numbers without multiplicatio.trace: 43-32 leaves 11 and sets quotient bit 2; 11-8 leaves 3 and sets bit 0; quotient 5, sign makes -5.
Divide two numbers without multiplicatio.pitfalls: Cast before abs to handle MIN_VALUE. b<<31 fits long for int magnitudes.

Power Set Bit Manipulation.problem: Enumerate positional subsets, including empty. Duplicate input values can create equal value lists.
Power Set Bit Manipulation.approach: A mask chooses each index independently. Every subset corresponds to exactly one n-bit mask.
Power Set Bit Manipulation.complexity: O(n*2^n) time and output storage; O(n) working subset.
Power Set Bit Manipulation.pitfalls: Java shifts mask counts; constrain n explicitly, and respect exponential memory. This teaching implementation limits n to 20.

XOR of numbers in a given range.problem: XOR all nonnegative integers in the inclusive range [l,r].
XOR of numbers in a given range.approach: Prefix XOR from 0 repeats a four-case cycle according to n mod 4. XOR two prefixes cancels all positions before l.
XOR of numbers in a given range.pitfalls: The formula is for nonnegative ordered bounds, not arbitrary signed intervals.

Set the i-th Bit.problem: Modify one zero-based bit in the signed 32-bit pattern and return the new pattern.
Set the i-th Bit.approach: OR sets, AND with an inverted mask clears, XOR toggles the addressed bit, leaving all others unchanged.
Set the i-th Bit.pitfalls: Validate index because Java shifts mask counts modulo32; bit31 may make the returned int negative.
